title: Vendor Minimal Access & Logging Agreement (Draft)
content:
Vendor Minimal Access & Logging Agreement (Draft)

Version: v0.1 (working draft)
Negotiation notes: see linked artifacts (Confluence + JIRA). This document is intended as a narrow contractual exhibit to be attached to vendor agreements where Redwood requires constrained access and explicit logging obligations for vendors who operate services that touch customer prompt or inference telemetry.

1. Purpose
The purpose of this Agreement is to define the minimum access privileges, mandatory logging and monitoring obligations, and audit-rights required of the Vendor in order to provide services that process or transit any Redwood customer data or telemetry. This agreement is intended to be incorporated into the Master Services Agreement (MSA) as an Exhibit.

2. Scope
Applies to: (a) Vendors operating inference services, telemetry collectors, or any tooling with the ability to view, store, or modify requests/responses, prompts, embeddings, model weights, or customer identifiers; (b) Subprocessors engaged by Vendor for the same.
Data types covered: prompts, model outputs, embeddings, request metadata (timestamps, IP), internal routing/trace identifiers, and associated configuration. Does not change broader privacy obligations in the MSA/DPA but sets operational controls.

3. Definitions
- "Minimal Access Principle": Vendor must configure systems such that humans and processes only have access to the least amount of data required to perform the task.
- "Protected Telemetry": Any logs, traces, or stored payloads that include or can be correlated to customer input or model outputs.
- "Audit Window": A minimum of 90 days for operational audit evidence unless otherwise agreed.

4. Minimum Access Controls
4.1 Role-Based Access: Vendor must implement RBAC enforcing least privilege. Administrative roles requiring access to Protected Telemetry must be restricted and approved by Vendor security.
4.2 Just-in-Time (JIT) Access: For human access to Protected Telemetry, Vendor must implement time-limited JIT elevation tied to an approver and recorded request (who/why/duration).
4.3 Access Reviews: Quarterly access reviews with evidence retained for the Audit Window. Evidence must include review outcome and remediation steps.

5. Authentication, Keys, and Secrets
5.1 MFA: All human accounts with any access to Protected Telemetry must be protected by MFA (OTP or hardware token).
5.2 Service Credentials: Long-lived credentials that allow access to Protected Telemetry are prohibited except where documented and rotated at least every 30 days.

6. Mandatory Logging & Monitoring
6.1 Logging Requirements: Vendor must log access events (read/write/delete) for all Protected Telemetry. Log fields must include: actor identity, timestamp (ISO8601), action, resource identifier, reason (if JIT), and correlation IDs for tracing.
6.2 Immutable Logs: Logs must be append-only and retained in a tamper-evident medium for the Audit Window.
6.3 Alerting: Vendor must configure alerts for anomalous access patterns (e.g., mass exports, off-hours bulk reads, more than X records accessed within Y minutes). Alert thresholds to be agreed in implementation plan.

7. Log Retention, Export, and Sharing
7.1 Retention: Default retention for Protected Telemetry access logs is 365 days unless shorter retention is required by specific customer contract; shorter retention requires Redwood written agreement.
7.2 Export for Forensics: Upon a Redwood request due to an incident, Vendor must export relevant log slices within 48 hours in a mutually agreed machine-readable format and preserve integrity.

8. Encryption and Key Management
8.1 Data at Rest: Protected Telemetry and logs must be encrypted at rest using industry standard algorithms (AES-256 or equivalent).
8.2 Data in Transit: TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers required for all network transit of Protected Telemetry and logs.
8.3 Key Custody: Customer-controlled key custody (bring-your-own-key) is strongly preferred for Private Deployment vendors. If Vendor manages keys, they must document HSM usage and rotation policy.

9. Incident Notification & Forensics
9.1 Notification Timeline: Vendor must notify Redwood within 24 hours of detection of any event that materially affects confidentiality or integrity of Protected Telemetry.
9.2 Forensic Support: Vendor must provide reasonable forensic assistance including timeline reconstructions, relevant exports, and a remediation plan. Costs for forensic work caused by Vendor negligence are Vendor's responsibility unless otherwise agreed.

10. Audit Rights & Evidence
10.1 Onsite/Remote Audits: Redwood reserves the right to conduct an annual remote audit of controls related to this Agreement and a for-cause audit following a material incident.
10.2 Evidence: Vendor must be able to produce: access lists, JIT approval records, RBAC policy snapshots, log hashes, and sample exports covering a rolling Audit Window.
10.3 Third-Party Attestations: SOC2 Type II or equivalent reports covering the control domains in scope are required annually; interim bridge letters accepted for pre-production vendors with an approved mitigation plan.

11. Subprocessors and Third Parties
Vendor must provide a list of subprocessors with the ability to access Protected Telemetry. Vendor will obtain written contractual commitments from subprocessors imposing obligations substantially similar to this Agreement. Redwood retains right to object to subprocessors for reasonable security/regulatory reasons.

12. Data Deletion and Return
12.1 Deletion on Termination: Upon termination or at Redwood's request, Vendor must delete or return Protected Telemetry within 30 days and provide a deletion certificate signed by a senior security officer.
12.2 Verification: Redwood may require Vendor to provide a sample proof of deletion for a reasonable subset of records.

13. Limitations & Liability
This Exhibit supplements but does not supersede the MSA's liability provisions. Where conflicts arise, parties should escalate to commercial and legal leads. Parties may negotiate liquidated damages for willful violations of access controls.

14. Survivability and Term
The obligations in this Agreement survive termination for a period equal to the longest retention period required by any Redwood customer contract, or three years, whichever is longer.

15. Governing Law
California law (as used in Redwood's MSA) unless otherwise negotiated in a specific SOW.

Appendix A — Implementation Checklist (negotiation guide)
- Confirm alert thresholds and examples.
- Decide default log retention (90/365/730 days).
- Agree JIT approval workflow/tooling and approver identity mapping.
- Define forensic export format (CSV/NDJSON) and schema.
- Decide whether key custody will be Vendor-managed or BYOK.
